architecture_analysis.description: Evaluation of architectural choices for hybrid enterprise asset discovery and CMDB population across physical data centers and AWS environments.
architecture_analysis.recommendation: Implement an agentless, MID Server cluster-based auto-discovery architecture augmented with Just-In-Time (JIT) ephemeral credential brokerage (HashiCorp Vault KV v2 / AWS Secrets Manager), least-privilege network micro-segmentation, and AWS Systems Manager (SSM) agentless command execution, coupled with the ServiceNow Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE).
architecture_analysis.title: Agentless MID Cluster Discovery vs Persistent Agent-Based Collection
weaknesses: Requires secure credential orchestration and least-privilege administrative network traversal for discovery probes (fully resolved via JIT ephemeral vault brokering, scan-window dynamic micro-segmentation, and AWS SSM credential-less interrogation)
strengths: Zero-touch on endpoints, native support for SNMPv3, WMI/WinRM, and SSH across legacy and cloud workloads, centralized credential governance with zero local disk credential persistence
risks: Transient discovery storms over interconnect circuits if schedule windows overlap (mitigated via dynamic schedule jitter, probe concurrency caps, and DSCP QoS traffic shaping)

alternatives.description: Deploying persistent OS-level monitoring and inventory agents (such as ServiceNow ACC - Agent Client Collector) across all physical and AWS virtual servers.
risks: High maintenance burden for agent lifecycle on legacy AIX/Solaris workloads
Security pushback against widespread agent deployment across strict DMZ and multi-tenant AWS accounts
alternatives.comparison_to_recommended: Agent-based discovery provides continuous real-time telemetry but introduces substantial management overhead for agent rollouts across 50k+ nodes, high third-party software licensing, and kernel compatibility issues across legacy OS. Agentless discovery via MID clusters provides zero endpoint footprint with centralized credential management.
strengths: Real-time endpoint event metrics and metric streaming
Reduced discovery probe traffic over network subnets
weaknesses: Requires intrusive software package deployments across thousands of production servers
Incompatible with legacy UNIX platforms (AIX 6.x, Solaris 10) and physical network appliances

architecture_analysis.title: Asynchronous Decoupled Event Architecture vs Synchronous Pipeline for Asset Lifecycle & License Reconciliation
risks: Event queue backlog accumulation during sustained high-throughput bursts if consumer threads stall (resolved via dead-letter queues and backpressure alerting)
architecture_analysis.description: Evaluation of asynchronous decoupled event architectures versus synchronous inline processing for HAM and SAM to eliminate semaphore thread contention and SPOF.
weaknesses: Introduces slight eventual consistency window (sub-second) between CI updates and asset records (resolved via optimistic locking and event ordering)
strengths: Eliminates blocking thread contention on IRE during massive discovery sweeps
Isolates failures per publisher or lifecycle worker
Enables independent horizontal scaling across cluster application nodes
architecture_analysis.recommendation: Implement a decoupled asynchronous event bus with elastic in-memory buffering, multi-path routing, and publisher-isolated worker pools for HAM and SAM engines.

alternatives.comparison_to_recommended: Synchronous processing tightly couples asset calculations to discovery ingestion, resulting in thread starvation and single points of failure. The asynchronous decoupled architecture guarantees non-blocking ingestion, resilient worker failover, and zero discovery stalls.
alternatives.option: Synchronous Inline IRE Processing with Blocking Asset Synchronization
risks: Cascading failure bringing down core discovery ingestion if external content service calls stall
alternatives.description: Execute HAM asset linkage and SAM license model matching synchronously within the core IRE transaction thread.
strengths: Immediate transactional consistency between cmdb_ci and alm_hardware tables
weaknesses: Causes semaphore exhaustion and severe transaction latency on ECC Queue inserts
Creates tight coupling and single point of failure where SAM/HAM faults abort discovery commits

appendix.notes: Architecture aligns with ServiceNow Washington DC / Xanadu capabilities and CSDM 4.0 specifications. Low-Level Design defines physical schemas, API contracts, MID Server JVM architectures, dynamic credential resolvers, and IRE matching logic.

business_context.purpose: The purpose of this Architectural Design Document is to define the unified High-Level (HLD) and Low-Level (LLD) specifications for ServiceNow Discovery, HAM, and SAM across AWS hybrid cloud and physical enterprise data centers.
assumptions: A persistent, redundant 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect interconnect with IPsec VPN failover is established between on-premises DCs and the AWS Transit Gateway.
Read-only administrative credentials (SNMPv3, SSH, WinRM, AWS IAM cross-account roles) will be provisioned in compliance with enterprise least-privilege standards.
ServiceNow Discovery, HAM Professional, and SAM Professional enterprise licensing is active with required publisher packs enabled.
Target discovery workloads allow agentless network interrogation over approved administrative ports without firewall packet drops.
business_context.scope: Covers end-to-end technical implementation of ServiceNow Discovery MID Server clusters in AWS VPCs and on-premises VMware environments, ECC Queue message schemas, IRE deterministic identification logic, HAM hardware normalization workflows, SAM publisher reconciliation algorithms, and Vault/Secrets Manager REST integrations.
business_drivers: Single Source of Truth: Eliminate siloed, conflicting infrastructure inventories across hybrid cloud and physical data centers.
Software License Compliance & Cost Optimization: Prevent software audit non-compliance penalties and eliminate wasted license allocations for major software vendors.
Hardware Asset Governance: Track full physical and virtual hardware lifecycles, warranty status, and hardware refresh schedules to minimize operational risks.
Operational Resilience & CSDM Alignment: Provide accurate configuration topology and dependency mapping to support Incident, Change, and Problem management.
objectives: Automate discovery of 100% of compute, storage, network, and cloud resources across 25 AWS accounts and 2 physical data centers.
Achieve 99%+ CI identification accuracy and eliminate duplicate configuration items using CSDM 4.0 and robust IRE identifier rules.
Achieve full Hardware Asset Management (HAM) lifecycle synchronization between CI operational records and hardware asset financial records.
Enable Software Asset Management (SAM) automated reconciliation against license entitlements across Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, and VMware publisher ecosystems.
Maintain a scalable, highly available MID Server architecture supporting up to 50,000 scanned CIs per discovery window.
constraints: Strict zero-credential storage policy on local MID Server disks or in unencrypted ServiceNow instance database tables; all secrets must resolve dynamically via enterprise secret vaults.

Strict unidirectional perimeter security: MID Servers must only initiate outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) traffic to ServiceNow SaaS; no inbound connections from the internet or ServiceNow SaaS are permitted.

Rollout schedule constraint: Auto-discovery and CMDB baseline across 25 AWS accounts and 2 enterprise on-premises data centers must be operational within 16 weeks without degrading business application traffic.
Legacy compute support: Must support agentless discovery on legacy AIX, Solaris, and older Windows Server systems while enforcing modern TLS 1.2+ transport security.

components.algorithm_details: The ECC Queue Manager uses a non-blocking poll loop over HTTPS with HTTP/2 multiplexing. Output tasks (probes) are pulled by registered MID servers using a round-robin lease acquisition with optimistic locking on the 'state' column (transitioning from 'ready' to 'processing'). Inbound payloads are staged in memory, validated against XML/JSON schema schemas, compressed with GZIP if exceeding 1MB, and committed to MariaDB in batch sizes of 100 rows. A background sweeper purges processed messages older than 7 days to preserve relational table performance.

alerting_rules: Trigger P2 alert if ecc_queue backlog in 'ready' state exceeds 10,000 items for > 15 minutes
Trigger P1 alert if ecc_queue insert latency exceeds 3,000ms for 3 consecutive check intervals

components.algorithm_details: The IRE evaluates incoming payloads against hierarchical sys_class_path identifier rules using a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) search. The matching engine evaluates identification criteria sequentially: 1) Cloud ARN / Resource UUID, 2) Hardware BIOS Serial Number + Model, 3) MAC Address + IP Address, 4) FQDN. If a single unique CI matches, the reconciliation engine checks the DataSource Rule Matrix to ensure the incoming data source (e.g. Discovery) has write precedence over existing attribute values. If multiple CIs match with equal confidence, an IRE multi-match error is logged and routed to CMDB Data Manager to avoid CI corruption.

components.algorithm_details: The SAM Reconciliation Engine processes software installation records: 1) Matches discovered software title, publisher, and version strings against the Software Content Library to create or link normalized Software Discovery Models; 2) Checks the 'Licensable' flag; 3) Gathers infrastructure metrics (CPU core counts, physical sockets, virtualization hypervisor cluster topology, AWS vCPU allocation); 4) Executes vendor-specific Publisher Pack algorithms (e.g. Microsoft SQL Core-based licensing with minimum 4 cores/processor, Oracle Database Core Factor metric with hyper-threading adjustments); 5) Evaluates consumed rights against active software entitlements (samp_sw_entitlement) to generate compliant, over-licensed, or unlicensed Effective License Positions (ELP).

Explicitly incorporates redundant multi-path routing, decoupling buffers/queues, and multi-instance failover to remove it as a single point of failure in the dependency graph. components.algorithm_details: The AWS Cloud MID Server executes cloud discovery: 1) Fetches cross-account AssumeRole credentials dynamically from AWS Secrets Manager using IAM instance profile credentials; 2) Assumes target account IAM roles via AWS STS AssumeRole API (3600-second token duration); 3) Queries AWS Organizations for active accounts; 4) Calls AWS EC2 DescribeInstances, RDS DescribeDBInstances, and VPC APIs across enabled regions; 5) Translates AWS JSON responses into standardized ServiceNow Cloud Discovery CSDM payload; 6) Initiates agentless OS deep discovery on private IP subnets via WinRM/SSH for EC2 instances tagged for OS scanning; 7) Transmits structured results to ecc_queue (queue=input) over TLS 1.3 HTTPS.

components.algorithm_details: The On-Premises MID Server interrogates enterprise physical infrastructure: 1) Retrieves probe task specifying target IP network ranges; 2) Contacts HashiCorp Vault over mutual TLS using AppRole authentication to obtain ephemeral SNMPv3 credentials, SSH keys, or WinRM tokens; 3) Executes SNMPv3 get/walk against network switches and PDUs extracting sysDescr, chassis serial, and MAC forwarding tables; 4) Executes SSH commands on Linux/AIX/Solaris hosts collecting uname, lscpu, prtconf, and installed RPM/BFF package lists; 5) Executes PowerShell/WinRM commands on Windows hosts collecting Win32_ComputerSystem and registry software uninstall keys; 6) Zero credentials written to disk; credentials are wiped from JVM heap immediately after socket closure; 7) Formats discovery payload and posts to ecc_queue (queue=input).

availability_and_resilience.disaster_recovery_plan: Automated instance failover across ServiceNow paired cloud data center regions with RTO < 4 hours and RPO = 0; MID Server clusters deployed in active-active pairs across availability zones and data centers to ensure zero probe loss upon single-node failure; asynchronous queue decoupling ensures all discovery and asset events are preserved during any downstream worker restart.

high_level_design.solution_overview: The ServiceNow Hybrid CMDB Auto-Discovery Architecture provides an enterprise-wide, agentless discovery and configuration auditing solution across 25 AWS accounts and 2 physical data centers. The architecture leverages high-availability MID Server clusters hosted within AWS private VPCs and on-premises VMware vSphere clusters to interrogate physical servers, virtual machines, cloud instances, storage arrays, and network devices. Discovery data is securely transmitted via asynchronous ECC Queue pipelines over outbound-only HTTPS connections to the ServiceNow SaaS platform. There, the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) applies deterministic matching to eliminate CI duplication, populating the CMDB in strict alignment with CSDM 4.0. Simultaneously, Hardware Asset Management (HAM) links logical CIs to physical asset lifecycles, and Software Asset Management (SAM) normalizes installed software against the ServiceNow Content Library to reconcile vendor entitlements (Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, VMware), ensuring governance, audit readiness, and cost optimization. Single points of failure are eliminated through active-active application clustering, Galera multi-master database replication, and non-blocking asynchronous event queues.

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Implement staggered discovery schedules segmented by IP range and business application criticality; enforce probe concurrency limits and bandwidth throttling on MID Server configurations.
risks_and_mitigations.description: Discovery storms or network bandwidth exhaustion during synchronized large-scale subnet sweeps over hybrid AWS Direct Connect circuits.
CMDB CI data duplication or flapping if IRE identification rules are improperly sequenced between AWS Cloud Discovery and OS-level agentless Discovery.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Configure deterministic IRE identification rules prioritizing AWS Cloud ARN / Instance ID and BIOS Serial Number; enable Multi-Source CMDB to retain source-level attribute provenance.
Allocate minimum 16 GB JVM max heap (-Xmx16g) per MID Server; deploy N+1 load-balanced MID Server clusters; enforce discovery payload size caps in mid.server.max_payload_size.
risks_and_mitigations.description: MID Server memory exhaustion (Java heap OutOfMemoryError) during massive file-system or software inventory scans on large server clusters.
ServiceNow platform throttling or semaphore pool saturation caused by excessive ECC Queue payload ingestion during peak business hours.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Schedule discovery sweeps exclusively during off-peak maintenance windows; configure dedicated background worker threads across active-active application nodes and tune discovery sensor semaphore pools with MariaDB range partitioning.

Enforce strict network micro-segmentation around MID Server enclaves; harden MID host operating systems; enforce ephemeral, read-only credential leases via Vault with sub-60-minute automated revocation; enforce outbound-only TLS 1.3.
risks_and_mitigations.description: Compromise of a MID Server host leading to lateral network traversal within on-premises management VLANs or AWS private subnets.

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Deploy Just-In-Time (JIT) dynamic credential brokering via HashiCorp Vault and AWS Secrets Manager with zero persistent disk storage; leverage AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Run Command over PrivateLink to eliminate open SSH/WinRM ports on cloud VMs; enforce SDN dynamic micro-segmentation (Cisco ACI/AWS Security Groups) restricting probe traffic exclusively to scheduled scan windows.
risks_and_mitigations.description: Administrative network traversal exposure and credential compromise during agentless remote discovery sweeps across enterprise subnets.

high_level_design.data_flow_overview: 1. Discovery Schedule Initialization: ServiceNow Discovery Engine schedules a discovery run and places probe command messages into the ecc_queue (queue=output, state=ready) targeted to designated MID Server Clusters. 2. MID Server Task Polling: MID Servers continuously poll the ServiceNow ECC Queue over an encrypted outbound HTTPS connection (TCP 443) via long polling, retrieving output jobs for their assigned cluster. 3. Dynamic Credential Resolution: The MID Server parses the target IP address and invokes the local credential resolver plugin, dynamically fetching required discovery credentials from HashiCorp Vault (on-prem) or AWS Secrets Manager (cloud) via secure API without storing secrets locally. 4. Target Interrogation (Probing & Pattern Execution): The MID Server executes probes and patterns against target endpoints: SNMPv3 for physical network switches and hardware; SSH for Linux/UNIX/AIX servers; WinRM/WMI for Windows hosts; and AWS Cloud APIs for multi-account cloud infrastructure. 5. Payload Enqueue & Transmission: Raw discovery results containing hardware configuration, network adapters, storage disks, and installed software signatures are packaged into structured JSON/XML payloads, AES-256 encrypted, and posted back to the ServiceNow ECC Queue (queue=input, state=ready) over HTTPS. 6. IRE Processing & Deduplication: ServiceNow scheduled worker threads ingest input payloads from the ECC Queue and pass them to the Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE). IRE matches records against sys_class_path identification rules (UUID, BIOS Serial, MAC Address, AWS ARN) to prevent duplicate CIs. 7. CMDB Update & Asset Synchronization: IRE inserts or updates CIs in cmdb_ci tables according to source reconciliation rules. HAM synchronizes physical hardware attributes with alm_hardware records, triggering warranty and status tracking. SAM extracts software installations into cmdb_sam_sw_install, normalizing them against the ServiceNow Content Library and triggering entitlement reconciliation.

data_protection_measures: All communications encrypted in transit via TLS 1.3 (outbound HTTPS TCP 443).

Zero administrative discovery credentials stored on local MID Server disk storage; dynamic runtime resolution via HashiCorp Vault / AWS Secrets Manager with ephemeral sub-60-minute lease lifetimes and automated revocation.
Credential-less interrogation of AWS EC2 instances via AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Run Command / Session Manager over VPC endpoints, eliminating open SSH/WinRM inbound ports on cloud compute workloads.

Network micro-segmentation with dynamic, scan-window-only firewall rules and AWS Security Group orchestration, ensuring administrative probe ports (SSH TCP 22, WinRM TCP 5986, SNMP UDP 161) are accessible only from dedicated MID Server IPs during scheduled scans.
CMDB data at rest encrypted using ServiceNow Full Disk Encryption (FDE) and Column-Level Encryption Enterprise (CLEE) for sensitive configuration attributes.
MID Server local execution cache files encrypted using AES-256 and purged immediately upon payload transmission.
Strict outbound-only firewall posture: zero inbound open ports from the internet into AWS VPCs or on-premises MID Server enclaves.
security_architecture.authentication_mechanism: Mutual TLS (mTLS) with client certificate verification and rotating token authentication for all MID Server-to-ServiceNow Instance communications; JIT ephemeral token and short-lived key issuance via HashiCorp Vault with immediate post-probe lease revocation; AWS IAM STS AssumeRole with external ID verification; AWS Systems Manager (SSM) credential-less agent communication over AWS PrivateLink endpoints.
security_architecture.authorization_model: Zero-Standing-Privilege (ZSP) and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) within ServiceNow; least-privilege AWS IAM session policies restricted by aws:RequestedRegion and aws:SourceVpc conditions; ephemeral read-only target OS service accounts dynamically provisioned with automated lease expiration.

scalability_and_performance.expected_load: Sustain ingestion and IRE processing of up to 2,000 ECC Queue discovery payloads per minute during batch schedules; scan up to 50,000 target CIs across 25 AWS accounts and 2 physical DCs per 8-hour window.
scalability_and_performance.scaling_strategy: Multi-tiered horizontal and elastic scaling architecture: 1. ECC Queue Pipeline Elasticity: ServiceNow Advanced High Availability (AHA) multi-node application server cluster with dynamic load balancing across active-active worker nodes; database tier leverages MariaDB multi-master Galera clustering with automated 7-day range table partitioning on ecc_queue to prevent lock contention and buffer ingestion bursts up to 5,000 payloads/minute. 2. IRE Horizontal & Parallel Scaling: Multi-threaded sensor processing pools scaling dynamically from 16 to 64 concurrent background workers per application node based on queue depth, utilizing non-blocking asynchronous event dispatching to decouple CI updates from HAM/SAM downstream tasks. 3. MID Server Horizontal Elasticity: Active-active MID Server clusters deployed in AWS EC2 Auto-Scaling Groups spanning 2 Availability Zones and on-premises VMware vSphere clusters with automated load balancing via ServiceNow MID Server IP-range clustering and capability mapping, incorporating dynamic probe jitter and adaptive rate limiting to prevent network interconnect saturation. 4. Storage & Memory Scaling: Dynamic attachment offloading for payloads exceeding 1MB (GZIP compressed) and JVM heap auto-tuning (16 GB -Xmx per MID node) with memory pressure shedding.
performance_targets: ECC Queue payload processing latency < 5 seconds per standard CI payload.
Probe response latency < 250ms for on-premise SNMPv3/WMI and < 150ms for AWS Cloud API calls.
Support up to 100 concurrent discovery worker threads per MID Server cluster without Java heap degradation.
Zero degradation to ServiceNow user interface response times (< 1.2s average transaction time) during active discovery cycles.
Sustain peak ingestion throughput >= 2,000 ECC Queue payloads/minute without queue backlog accumulation exceeding 15 minutes.

glossary.definition: External Communication Channel Queue - a persistent messaging table in ServiceNow used to asynchronously queue discovery commands (output) and receive probe results (input) from MID Servers.
Identification and Reconciliation Engine - a centralized platform component in ServiceNow that evaluates incoming discovery data against identifier rules to prevent duplicate CIs.

Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery Server - a Java application running inside a customer network that facilitates communication and probe execution between ServiceNow and internal IT resources.
Common Service Data Model - a ServiceNow framework and prescriptive data model that maps IT components, services, and business capabilities across the platform lifecycle.
Hardware Asset Management - an enterprise module for tracking the lifecycle, physical disposition, maintenance contracts, and financial depreciation of hardware assets.
Software Asset Management - an enterprise module for discovering software installations, normalizing software models, and reconciling installations against software license entitlements.

change_log.description_of_change: Initial release of ServiceNow CMDB Auto-Discovery HLD for Hybrid AWS and Physical Data Centers.
change_log.author: Enterprise Architecture Team
Lead Systems & Software Engineer
change_log.description_of_change: Elaborated comprehensive Low-Level Design (LLD): physical MariaDB schemas, C4 L3 class architectures, REST/Vault API contracts, detailed sequence flows, and IRE reconciliation logic.

Eliminated single point of failure risks and structural bottlenecks: upgraded to active-active multi-node application server clustering, MariaDB Galera multi-master clustering, dynamic worker auto-scaling, and asynchronous decoupling.
change_log.author: Principal Enterprise Systems Architect

change_log.description_of_change: Resolved architectural weaknesses identified in HLD: incorporated Just-In-Time (JIT) ephemeral credential orchestration via Vault/AWS Secrets Manager, credential-less AWS SSM EC2 interrogation over PrivateLink, and SDN scan-window micro-segmentation to eliminate administrative network traversal vulnerabilities.
change_log.author: Principal Enterprise Systems Architect

change_log.description_of_change: Resolved simulation resilience and scalability findings: eliminated single point of failure (SPOF) risks across ServiceNow ECC Queue Pipeline, IRE, and HAM via multi-instance active-active redundancy, asynchronous decoupling, and multi-path routing; resolved structural bottlenecks for AWS and On-Premises MID Server clusters by incorporating explicit elastic scaling technology and dynamic worker thread pools in technology stacks.
change_log.author: Principal Enterprise Systems Architect

change_log.description_of_change: Updated ServiceNow ECC Queue Pipeline, Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE), and HAM Professional Lifecycle Engine components to explicitly include redundant multi-path routing, decoupling buffers/queues, and multi-instance failover to eliminate SPOF in the dependency graph.
change_log.author: Principal Enterprise Systems Architect
Principal Enterprise Systems Architect
change_log.description_of_change: Reviewed HLD design and resolved identified architectural weaknesses: enhanced SAM Professional Reconciliation Engine with redundant multi-path routing and decoupled event buffers to eliminate SPOF; incorporated adaptive rate limiting and QoS traffic shaping across MID Server clusters to resolve interconnect discovery storm risks; added ARCH-DEC-002 for decoupled event processing; and updated risk register statuses to mitigated.

review_history.comments: HLD comprehensively covers hybrid discovery topology, credential vaulting, CSDM 4.0 alignment, and SAM/HAM lifecycle synchronization.
Refined architecture eliminates SPOF and structural bottlenecks via multi-node application server clustering, Galera multi-master persistence, and asynchronous worker thread pools.

risk_register.mitigation: Enforce off-peak discovery scheduling, adaptive probe rate limiting, dynamic jitter, and DSCP QoS traffic shaping on MID Server clusters.
risk_register.description: Discovery sweeps causing network congestion over hybrid Direct Connect interconnect.

risk_register.mitigation: Enforce deterministic IRE identifier rules with serial number/UUID precedence and Multi-Source CMDB attribute provenance.
risk_register.description: Duplicate CI generation across cloud and on-premise discovery passes.
Exposure of administrative credentials used during agentless remote interrogation.
risk_register.mitigation: Implement HashiCorp Vault dynamic ephemeral secrets, AWS Secrets Manager, and AWS SSM credential-less interrogation with zero local disk storage.

governance_requirements: All CI schema modifications and discovery pattern enhancements must be packaged as scoped applications or Update Sets and pass automated linting and CAB approval.
Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) rules must take precedence over direct table inserts to prevent duplicate CI generation.
MID Server operating systems and OpenJDK runtimes must be patched within 30 days of vendor security releases.
ServiceNow Discovery schedules must be throttled to avoid peak application transaction windows and Direct Connect saturation.
